title: Our new XR e-book is here: Build XR with Unity: Meta XR
summary: Download the free Build XR with Unity: Meta XR e-book. Learn eye and hand tracking, 5K display optimization, and AI-assisted workflows for Meta VR Glasses.
body_markdown:
Clicking through Editor panels can become a bottleneck for repetitive tasks and automation. The new Unity CLI and Unity Pipeline package give both developers and AI agents a fast, lightweight command-line interface into the Unity Editor. The Pipeline package turns the running Editor into a local background server, so scenes and asset databases stay warm in memory and there's no cold-start boot for every command.


Any agent that can run shell commands, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI, can control the Editor, build your app, and help fix errors. Unity's official plugins for[Claude](https://unity.com/blog/unity-plugin-codex) and[Codex](https://unity.com/blog/unity-plugin-codex) teach agents to do jobs the way Unity workflows are meant to work, and install 29 skills with a single command at launch.


To close the loop, Meta XR Operator lets an agent act inside the running XR app: inspect the scene, move the head, controllers, and hands, perform gestures like pinch, poke, and grab (including gaze-and-pinch for Meta VR Glasses), and capture the rendered view to verify the result. It's an experimental component, so use it for development and testing rather than as a production dependency, and keep testing comfort, tracking, and performance on physical hardware.


## **Download the e-book**


Ready to Build for Meta VR Glasses? Download[Build XR with Unity: Meta XR](https://unity.com/resources/build-xr-with-unity-meta-xr) to get the full step-by-step walkthrough, including the interactive scene tutorial and links to samples, video tutorials, and Unity Learn resources.
